senses.sense_definition: To respond to a gesture, action, or emotion with a corresponding or equivalent one.

examples.text: When they invited us over for dinner, we <w>reciprocated</w> by bringing dessert.
He offered his full friendship, but she unfortunately did not <w>reciprocate</w> his feelings.

senses.sense_definition: To mutually exchange goods, favors, or privileges between two parties.

examples.text: Both nations agreed to lower trade barriers and <w>reciprocate</w> economic concessions.
The partner institution promised to <w>reciprocate</w> benefits for our visiting researchers.

senses.sense_definition: To respond negatively to an attack, insult, or hostile act; to retaliate.

examples.text: Rather than diffuse the argument, he chose to <w>reciprocate</w> with harsh accusations.
If provoked further by aggressive tariffs, the government warned that it would promptly <w>reciprocate</w>.

synonyms: give as good as one gets

senses.sense_definition: To alternate backward and forward or up and down in linear motion.

examples.text: The mechanical piston begins to <w>reciprocate</w> smoothly inside the combustion cylinder.
Modern cutting saws often feature a blade designed to rapidly <w>reciprocate</w> through timber.
